etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English crispy; equivalent to crisp +‎ -y.

definitions.definition: Having a crisp texture; brittle yet tender.

quote.citation: 1671, Tho[mas] Jordan, London’s Resurrection to Joy and Triumph, Expressed in Sundry Shews, Shapes, Scenes, Speeches, and Songs in Parts; […], London:  […] Henry Brome […], page 3:
quote.text: […] on his Head a long and criſpy hair, […]

definitions.definition: (informal) The well-baked fat on the surface of a piece of roasted meat.
